q: Use the first four terms of the binomial expansion of $(1 - \frac{1}{50})^{\frac{1}{2}}$ to derive the approximation $\sqrt{2} \approx 1.414214$. Calculate similarly an approximation to the cube root of 2 to six decimal places by considering $(1 + \frac{N}{125})^{\frac{1}{3}}$, where $N$ is a suitable number. [You need not justify the accuracy of your approximations.]

How many integers greater than or equal to zero and less than 1000 are not divisible by 2 or 5? What is the average value of these integers? How many integers greater than or equal to zero and less than 9261 are not divisible by 3 or 7? What is the average value of these integers?
answer: First part: 400 integers, with average 500 (pairing or symmetry). Second part: 5292 integers, with average $9261/2$ (pairing or symmetry), using blocks of 21 in which 12 integers are not divisible by 3 or 7.

q: How many integers greater than or equal to zero and less than $(pq)^3$ are not divisible by $p$ or $q$? What is the average value of these integers?
Sketch the following subsets of the $x$-$y$ plane: (i) $|x| + |y| \leqslant 1$; (ii) $|x - 1| + |y - 1| \leqslant 1$; (iii) $|x - 1| - |y + 1| \leqslant 1$; (iv) $|x|\,|y - 2| \leqslant 1$.
answer: Part (i): in the first quadrant the region is $x + y \leqslant 1$, i.e. the region below the line $x+y=1$. The other quadrants follow by symmetry, since the inequality is unchanged when $x$ is replaced by $-x$ or $y$ by $-y$. Parts (ii) to (iv) are obtained by translating the origin as appropriate.
